name: live-bank read audit
method: Read-only SQL against the live production bank (Postgres 127.0.0.1:5433, db pseudolife_memory) via docker exec psql. Ad-hoc queries; this audit motivated the schema v33 read-telemetry change that productizes them as memory_stats read_audit.
caveats: access_count counts an entry surfacing in a final memory_search/memory_get result set (cms.py access accrual), not proof the agent used it; every search bumps its full served top-k.
Counts sync to PG on the save cadence, so very recent accesses may lag.
Eviction had never fired (765 of 5000 flat-band capacity), so the age gradient is genuine recall traffic, not survivorship.

External comparison baseline: Theo (t3.gg), 'Turn off Claude Code's Memory', 2026-08, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jf54k7tFeEc - 45 auto-memories in one project clone, 26 (58%) never read once, 19 sessions read vs 80 wrote (~1:3 read:write). Different instrument (file opens vs search surfacing), so directionally comparable only.

facts.read_signal: none - fact slot reads were untracked pre-v33 (memory_traces is provenance, last_confirmed is write-side); this gap is what slot_reads closes

reinforcements_note: entries.reinforcements conflated explicit memory_reinforce with automatic dream-trace bumps (service.py dream_run trace path), so 562 reinforced entries measured consolidation yield (73% of entries fed at least one cortex fact), not usefulness; the v33 explicit_reinforcements column splits this going forward.
